text:
My girlfriend went to get a filling/dental treatment.
The dentist said it could be filled, so she agreed. The dentist then cut into her gums.
After a while, they said it needed to be extracted and took her for a new X-ray.
Shouldn't the X-ray have been done from the start, and the patient informed about the procedure, including the possibility of extraction, so they could make an informed decision? Instead, they cut into her gums first.
Once the dentist said it needed to be extracted, she had no choice but to accept it.
My girlfriend saw the dentist from around 5 PM until almost 8 PM. She came out with pain, swelling, and a torn mouth.
She had to keep her mouth open for 3 hours. General dentists usually don't recommend extraction if the root is still strong and the tooth isn't decayed.
This is incredibly strange but true. I'm giving it 1 star. I really didn't want to give any stars if this is how a clinic operates.
